questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people blush when they are shy
How to become a doctor
Funny stories about meeting parents
How embarrassment can stop people getting medical help
questions.why: They discuss medical embarrassment, when people feel too embarrassed to see a doctor.

options: He forgot where he had parked his parents' car in a big car park
He waved excitedly at a couple he thought were his parents
He answered the phone in a silly voice
He fell over in front of his friends
questions.why: He waved his hands in a silly way at a car, then discovered it was another couple.

questions.q: Why was Beth embarrassed when she answered the phone?
options: She forgot her best friend's name when she answered the phone
Her dad was listening
She used a silly voice, but the caller wasn't her friend
She was talking to a doctor
questions.why: She said hello in a silly voice thinking it was her best friend, but they asked to speak to her dad.

questions.q: According to Beth, when do people usually feel embarrassed?
options: When they feel different from others, especially physically
When they are spending time with close friends and members of their family
Only when they are ill
When they are very tired
questions.why: She says we get embarrassed if we feel different from others, especially if the difference is physical.

questions.q: What does Dr Vanessa Apea say happens because of embarrassment?
options: People delay treatment, so problems are found much later
People visit the doctor too often
Doctors refuse to see some patients who are too embarrassed to speak
Patients ask for too many tests
questions.why: She says people delay seeking treatment and could have been diagnosed much earlier.

questions.q: Which idea for patients does Dr Apea NOT recommend?
options: Writing the problem down
Going with a friend
Searching online instead of seeing a doctor
Seeing a doctor that you already know well and trust
questions.why: Her ideas are writing it down, going with a friend and visiting a doctor you trust.

questions.q: Why does Dr Apea tell patients in advance that she'll ask personal questions?
options: To save time
To help them feel relaxed and safe by being open
Because the law says she must
So they can prepare written answers before the appointment starts
questions.why: She brings transparency and assures them it's a confidential, safe, non-judgmental space.

questions.q: What else does Dr Apea use to help patients relax?
options: Relaxing music in her office
A friendly nurse who stays in the room during the examination
Short, simple medical words
Her facial expressions, gestures and tone of voice
questions.why: She uses non-verbal cues – her face, hand movements and tone of voice.
